To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maternal consumption of the probiotic bacteriun Lactobacillius plantarum 29v affects gastrointestinal growth, function and immune development in the suckling offspring.
maternal exposure to the probiotic bacterion Lactobacilli plantarum 29v affects gastrointestinal growth in the suckling offspring.
maternal consumption of Lact. plantarum 29v during pregnancy and lactation affects gut growth, function and immune development in the offspring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects on the gastrointestinal tract of the newborn rat when the dam is exposed to the Gram-positive bacterium, L. plantarum 29v, during the pregnancy period and during lactation.
the impact of maternal exposure to probiotic bacteria on the gut development and function of suckling offspring.
the role of the maternal gut microflora in the development of gut function in the offspring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results reported here show that manipulating the microflora by giving expecting mothers a probiotic strain, Lactobabillus plantarum, prior to parturution and during lactation affects the growth and function of the gut in the offspring.

the probiotic strain Lactobacillu s plantarum  299v, when given to pregnant and lacta ting dams in their drinking water, affects the growth and function of the gastrointestinal tract in suckling rat pups.
maternal consumption of Lp299v during pregnancy and lactation leads to an altered GI growth and function in their pups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the maternal gut microbiota is important for the gut growth and maturation in the suckling offspring.
Lp299 v is able to colonize both the mother and the pups and that this colonization affects the pups' gut growth and function during the first weeks of life.
the gut microbiota of the mother is able to colonize her offspring and that the gut microbiome of the offspring is able to affect the gut growth and gut function of the offspring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut microbiome is not a static community but is rather dynamic and can change in response to external influences.
the gut microbiota of the mother is an important source for the development of the offspring's gut microbiota, which in turn affects the development of the gut and the immune system in the offspring.
the gut microflora is important for the development of the gut and the immune system, which may have implications for the prevention of diseases in the offspring.
